:::{#thm-square-of-a-sum}
#### Square of a sum

For any numbers $a$ and $b$,

$$
(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2
$$

:::

::: proof
By @sol-square-of-a-sum.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-square-of-a-difference}
#### Square of a difference

Replacing $b$ by $-b$ in @thm-square-of-a-sum
gives $(a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2$.
Squared errors such as $(y - \hat{y})^2$ are expanded this way.
For example, with $y = 5$ and $\hat{y} = 3$,
$(5 - 3)^2 = 2^2 = 4$,
and $5^2 - 2 \cdot 5 \cdot 3 + 3^2 = 25 - 30 + 9 = 4$.

:::
